topic: Change of Basis in Linear Algebra

sections.title: Prerequisites: The Language of Vectors
lecture_lines: A basis defines our coordinate system.
Vectors are displacements, not just numbers.
Coordinates depend on the basis chosen.
animations: Create two orthogonal unit vectors in #FFFFFF labeled 'i' and 'j'.
Animate a vector 'v' as a linear combination of 'i' and 'j' in #FFFF00.
Highlight the scalar coefficients as the vector coordinates.

sections.title: The Problem: Viewing Space from Different Angles
lecture_lines: View the same vector from different angles.
Basis B and Basis C are perspectives.
We need a bridge between these views.
animations: Display a grid with basis 'B' in #00FFFF and 'C' in #FF00FF.
Show a point 'P' and its different coordinate representations.
Emphasize the distance between representation 'P_B' and 'P_C'.

sections.title: Constructing the Transition Matrix
lecture_lines: Express new basis vectors as old ones.
These become columns of matrix P.
P maps new coordinates to standard.
Grid lines warp to the new basis.
Now we have our transition machine.
animations: Represent basis 'B' vectors as columns in a matrix 'M' in #FFFF00.
Visualize 'M' transforming the standard basis into basis 'B'.
Flash the matrix columns to link with 'B' basis vectors.
Warp the grid lines to illustrate the basis transformation.
Highlight the finished transition matrix 'M' as a tool.

sections.title: The Change of Basis Formula: The Transformation
lecture_lines: Use robots to navigate local frames.
Map local movement to global space.
animations: Show 'v_B = P * v_C' formula in #FFFFFF with clear labels.
Animate the transition matrix 'P' shifting the coordinate space.
Animate 'P' inverse reversing the coordinate mapping.
Use a robot graphic to show movement in local frames.
Draw arrows mapping local movement into global vector space.

sections.title: Summary & Application
lecture_lines: We only change our coordinate description.
Grid lines rotate, labels update accordingly.
animations: Display a recap of the 'Change of Basis' formula in #FFFFFF.
Show a real-world rotation coordinate shift in 2D space.
Fade out with the key takeaway: 'Perspective changes'.
